See also: Ballerina

English

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Italian ballerina.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˌbæləɹˈiːnə/
  • Audio (Southern England):(file)
  • Rhymes: -iːnə

Noun

[edit]

ballerina (plural ballerinas or ballerine)

  1. (nonstandard) A ballet dancer (unisex term)
    1. (often) A female ballet dancer.
      1. Ellipsis of prima ballerina (“the star female ballet performer in the company”).
        Synonyms: prima ballerina, prima donna, prima
    2. (less common, nonstandard) A male ballet dancer; Synonym of ballerino.
  2. A ballet flat shoe.

Usage notes

[edit]

Although normally used to refer only to females, it can be used of males although this is sometimes done so derogatorily. Danseur or ballet dancer is the normal term for men.

Derived terms

[edit]
  • ballerinadom
  • ballerinalike
  • gallerina
  • prima ballerina

Related terms

[edit]
  • ballerino

Finnish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Italian ballerina.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈbɑlːeri(ː)nɑ/, [ˈbɑ̝lːe̞ˌri(ː)nɑ̝]
  • Rhymes: -inɑ
  • Syllabification(key): bal‧le‧ri‧na
  • Hyphenation(key): bal‧le‧ri‧na

Noun

[edit]

ballerina

  1. (dance) ballerina (female ballet dancer)
    Synonym: balettitanssijatar
  2. ballet flat, dolly flat (type of women's shoes, with a very low heel, low sides and covering only the toes)
    Synonyms: ballerinakenkä, ballerinatossu
